While the 90% confidence intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, certain major, unforeseen events could push actual results beyond these bounds. These include so-called "black swan" events such as unexpected geopolitical crises, widespread natural disasters, or sudden, severe economic shocks that drastically alter market conditions. Additionally, radical technological breakthroughs or disruptions, significant and unforeseen shifts in regulatory policy, or a major change in the fundamental supply and demand dynamics of the forecast variable could lead to outcomes far outside the anticipated range. These events represent systemic changes or extreme volatility that are not typically accounted for in standard probabilistic models.
